title.en: What's Your Constitution? Know Your Dosha, Read Your Body's Language
title.zh: 你是哪种体质？认识你的 Dosha，读懂你的身体语言

content.en:
Have you ever had this feeling —
your body has been speaking to you all along, but you just can't understand its language?
Lower back pain today, tight shoulders tomorrow. Some nights you can't sleep; other nights you sleep for hours and still wake up exhausted. You've tried everything — massage, stretching, a new pillow — and sometimes it helps a little. But that underlying pattern? It never really goes away.
This isn't your fault. You simply haven't yet learned your body's unique language.
Within the wisdom of Ayurveda, there is a key that can help you decode these patterns. It's called your Dosha.

What is a Dosha?

Ayurveda is a life science originating in India with over 5,000 years of history. Ayur means "life," Veda means "knowledge" — together, it is a complete system for living in harmony with life itself.

Ayurveda holds that the natural world is made up of five great elements: Ether, Air, Fire, Water, and Earth. Inside our bodies, these five elements combine in three distinct ways to form our unique constitution — the Tridosha:

Vata (Air + Ether) — governs movement, breath, and the nervous system
Pitta (Fire + Water) — governs digestion, metabolism, and transformation
Kapha (Earth + Water) — governs structure, lubrication, and stability

Every person is born with all three Doshas — just in different proportions. This unique ratio is your innate constitution, known in Ayurveda as your Prakriti.

When your Doshas are in balance, you feel vibrant, clear-minded, and light in your body. When they fall out of balance, your body begins to send signals — through pain, tension, emotional shifts, digestive issues, and disrupted sleep — telling you: hey, something here needs your attention.

The Three Constitutions

Vata — Child of the Wind
Elements: Air + Ether | Governs: movement, breath, nervous system

Vata types are like the wind — light, flowing, and endlessly creative. Your mind leaps from thought to thought, inspiration arrives in flashes, and you are a natural creator and explorer. You have an innate sensitivity to beauty, art, and music, and your capacity to feel runs deeper than most people realise.

When Vata is balanced, you are:
An inspired creator, eloquent and expressive, mentally flexible and open, light and energetic in spirit

When Vata is imbalanced, you may experience:
Anxiety and indecision, light and dream-filled sleep, feeling cold easily, irregular digestion, difficulty finishing what you start

Vata physical traits:
Slender build with visible joints, dry skin and hair, hands and feet that tend to run cold

Pitta — Messenger of Fire
Elements: Fire + Water | Governs: digestion, metabolism, transformation

Pitta types are like fire — intense, focused, and driven by clear direction. You are a natural leader with a strong sense of purpose and the ability to execute. Your digestive fire is powerful — not just for food, but for information and experience too. You carry a deep hunger for truth and understanding.

When Pitta is balanced, you are:
A wise and inspiring leader, organised and efficient, deeply passionate and purposeful

When Pitta is imbalanced, you may experience:
Irritability and impatience, perfectionism, skin inflammation and redness, acid reflux, restless sleep, excessive self-criticism and criticism of others

Pitta physical traits:
Medium, well-proportioned build with defined muscle tone, oily skin prone to redness, higher body temperature, strong appetite

Kapha — Guardian of the Earth
Elements: Earth + Water | Governs: structure, lubrication, stability

Kapha types are like the earth itself — grounded, deeply caring, and nourishing by nature. You are the most loyal and steadfast presence in any relationship; people feel safe and loved simply by being near you. Your endurance is remarkable, and your memory is exceptional — once you truly learn something, it stays with you for life.

When Kapha is balanced, you are:
A loving and patient nurturer, steady and reliable, with extraordinary memory and physical resilience

When Kapha is imbalanced, you may experience:
Heaviness and stagnation, procrastination, emotional eating, excessive sleep, resistance to change, attachment to the past

Kapha physical traits:
Fuller, rounded build with smooth and well-moisturised skin, stable joints, strong endurance with a slow start

Understanding Dosha Through the Lens of Fascia

As a teacher who has worked with fascia and body healing for many years, I've discovered something that continues to fascinate me:
Every Dosha imbalance corresponds to a specific pattern of fascial tension.

Our fascia — the connective tissue network that envelops every muscle, organ, and nerve in the body — is far more than a physical structure. It is a repository of emotion and a map of constitutional energy.

When you begin to look at your fascia through the lens of Dosha, the pain in your body starts to make sense.

The Fascial Language of Vata Imbalance

When Vata is imbalanced, the fascia presents as migratory tension — pain here today, tightness there tomorrow, with no fixed source. Joints click and pop, muscles seize without warning, and the whole body carries a quality of "drifting," unable to truly root into the present moment.

This is wind fascia: taut, yet with nowhere to land.
Your fascia is craving the weight of the earth — to be held with warmth and steadiness.

The Fascial Language of Pitta Imbalance

When Pitta is imbalanced, the fascia presents as inflammatory tension — a burning sensation in the neck and shoulders, a jaw that habitually clenches, muscles braced as though always preparing for battle. This tension carries a quality of "can't let go": to release feels like losing control, like imperfection.

This is fire fascia: hot, rigid, unable to stop.
Your fascia is craving permission to rest — permission to not try so hard.

The Fascial Language of Kapha Imbalance

When Kapha is imbalanced, the fascia presents as stagnant tension — a pervasive heaviness throughout the body, the greatest difficulty arising in the morning, connective tissue that has become adhesive and slow-moving. This tension isn't painful exactly; it's more like an indescribable sense of being stuck.

This is earth fascia: dense, sluggish, unable to feel light.
Your fascia is craving warm movement — to be gently, tenderly awakened.

Your Constitution Is Not Your Fate

There is one point I want to make clearly:
Coming to know your Dosha is not about labelling yourself.

Ayurveda is not a system of fate — it is a navigational tool. Understanding your constitution helps you make better choices for yourself in each moment: what to eat, how to move, what kind of rest you need, and which environments allow you to truly flourish.

And remember — each of us is a blend of all three Doshas. Many people have two dominant constitutions (such as Vata-Pitta or Pitta-Kapha), and very few people are balanced across all three equally.

Most importantly, your Dosha shifts with the seasons, your age, stress levels, diet, and lifestyle. This is what makes Ayurveda so beautiful — it is living wisdom, not fixed rules.

Starting a Conversation with Your Body

Now that you know the three constitutions, what comes next?
Not an immediate overhaul of everything.
I always tell my students: begin with observation.

Today, simply notice:
Where does your body most often hold tension?
Is that tension migratory, burning, or heavy?
When you're under pressure, what is your first response — anxiety, anger, or withdrawal?

These observations are your first step toward reading your body's language.

"The body never lies. It's simply waiting for you to learn its language."

The first time I encountered Ayurveda, I realised that everything in my body that I'd never quite been able to explain — that wandering tension, that constant sense of drifting, that bone-deep exhaustion no amount of sleep could touch — finally had a name.

With a name comes direction. And with direction, true healing can begin.
content.zh:
有没有一种感觉——
你的身体一直在说话，但你听不懂它的语言？
今天腰痛，明天肩膀紧，有时候睡不着，有时候怎么睡都睡不够。你试过很多方法：按摩、伸展、换枕头……有时好一点，但那个根本的模式，始终还在。
这不是你的错。你只是还没有学会你身体独特的语言。
在阿育吠陀的智慧里，有一把钥匙，能帮你读懂这些模式。它叫做 Dosha。

什么是 Dosha？

阿育吠陀（Ayurveda）是源自印度、超过5000年历史的生命科学。Ayur 是「生命」，Veda 是「知识」——它是一套关于如何与生命和谐共存的完整系统。

阿育吠陀相信，自然界由五大元素构成：空、风、火、水、土。在我们的身体里，这五种元素以三种不同的方式组合，就形成了我们独特的体质——三督夏（Tridosha）：

Vata（风 + 空）——掌管动作、呼吸、神经系统
Pitta（火 + 水）——掌管消化、代谢、转化
Kapha（土 + 水）——掌管结构、润滑、稳定

每个人天生都有这三种 Dosha，只是比例不同。这个独特的比例，就是你的先天体质（Prakriti）。

当你的 Dosha 处于平衡状态，你感到充满活力、思路清晰、身体轻盈。当它失衡，身体就会开始发出信号——通过疼痛、紧绷、情绪、消化和睡眠问题，告诉你：嘿，有什么东西需要你的注意了。

认识三种体质

Vata — 风的孩子
元素：风 + 空 ｜ 掌管：动作、呼吸、神经系统

Vata 体质的人像风一样——轻盈、流动、充满创意。你的思维跳跃，灵感不断，你是天生的创造者和探索者。你对美、艺术、音乐有天然的敏感度，感受能力比旁人深刻得多。

当 Vata 平衡时，你是：
充满灵感的创造者、语言表达流畅、思维灵活开放、能量轻盈跳跃

当 Vata 失衡时，你会：
焦虑、游移不定、睡眠浅而多梦、容易感到冷、肠胃不规律、难以完成开始的事情

Vata 的身体特征：
体型偏纤细、骨节明显、皮肤干燥、头发容易干枯、手脚经常偏凉

Pitta — 火的使者
元素：火 + 水 ｜ 掌管：消化、代谢、转化

Pitta 体质的人像火一样——炽热、专注、充满方向感。你是天生的领导者，目标明确，执行力强。你的消化力旺盛，不只是对食物，对信息和经验也是。你有强烈的追求真相的渴望。

当 Pitta 平衡时，你是：
充满智慧的领导者、条理清晰、高效执行、充满激情与目标感

当 Pitta 失衡时，你会：
容易急躁、完美主义、皮肤泛红发炎、胃灼热、睡眠浅而烦躁、对自己和他人过度苛求

Pitta 的身体特征：
体型中等匀称、肌肉轮廓明显、皮肤偏油容易泛红、体温偏高、食欲旺盛

Kapha — 大地的守护者
元素：土 + 水 ｜ 掌管：结构、润滑、稳定

Kapha 体质的人像大地一样——稳重、深情、充满滋养力。你是关系里最忠诚的守护者，你的存在让周围的人感到安心与被爱。你有极好的耐力和记忆力，一旦学会的东西，终生不忘。

当 Kapha 平衡时，你是：
充满爱与耐心的滋养者、稳定踏实、记忆力惊人、身体抵抗力强

当 Kapha 失衡时，你会：
感到沉重与停滞、拖延、情绪性进食、过度睡眠、难以改变、执着于过去

Kapha 的身体特征：
体型丰满圆润、皮肤光滑湿润、关节稳定、体力持久但启动慢

从筋膜的角度，重新理解 Dosha

作为一名从事筋膜与身体疗愈工作多年的老师，我发现了一件让我着迷的事：
每一种 Dosha 的失衡，都对应着特定的筋膜紧绷模式。

我们的筋膜——包覆全身每一块肌肉、每一个器官、每一根神经的结缔组织网络——不只是物理结构。它是情绪的储存库，也是体质能量的地图。

当你开始用 Dosha 的眼光看你的筋膜，身体的疼痛开始变得有意义。

Vata 失衡的筋膜语言

Vata 失衡时，筋膜呈现游走性紧绷——今天这里痛，明天那里紧，找不到固定的来源。关节会咔咔响，肌肉会突然痉挛，整个身体有一种「飘离感」，难以真正扎根于当下。

这是风的筋膜：绷紧却无处着力。
你的筋膜在渴望大地的重量，渴望被温暖、稳定地握住。

Pitta 失衡的筋膜语言

Pitta 失衡时，筋膜呈现炎症性紧绷——肩颈有灼热感，颌关节习惯性咬紧，肌肉过度用力，好像时刻准备战斗。这种紧绷带着一种「不能放开」的特质：松开就会失控，就会不完美。

这是火的筋膜：热、硬、无法停下来。
你的筋膜在渴望被允许休息，被允许不那么努力。

Kapha 失衡的筋膜语言

Kapha 失衡时，筋膜呈现沉滞性紧绷——全身有一种厚重的沉重感，早晨特别难以启动，结缔组织粘连，流动性变差。这种紧绷没有疼痛感，只有一种难以形容的「卡住」。

这是土的筋膜：厚重、滞涩、无法轻盈。
你的筋膜在渴望温暖的流动，渴望被温柔地唤醒。

你的体质，不是你的命运

这里有一点很重要，我想特别说明：
认识你的 Dosha，不是为了给自己贴标签。

阿育吠陀不是一套命运系统，它是一套导航工具。你了解自己的体质，是为了更懂得如何在每一个当下做出对自己最好的选择——吃什么、怎么动、需要什么样的休息、在什么样的关系里最能绽放。

而且，我们每个人都是三种 Dosha 的混合。很多人有两种主导体质（比如 Vata-Pitta 或 Pitta-Kapha），极少数人三种均衡。

更重要的是，你的 Dosha 会随着季节、年龄、压力、饮食和生活方式而变化。这正是阿育吠陀美丽的地方——它是活的智慧，不是死的规则。

用你的体质，开始与身体对话

了解了三种体质之后，下一步是什么？
不是立刻改变一切。
我总是告诉我的学生：从观察开始。

今天，只是注意：
你的身体最常在哪里紧绷？
那种紧绷是游走的、灼热的，还是沉重的？
当你压力大的时候，你的第一个反应是焦虑、愤怒，还是退缩？

这些观察，就是你开始读懂自己身体语言的第一步。

"身体从不说谎。它只是在等你学会它的语言。"

当我第一次接触阿育吠陀，我才意识到，我身体里所有「说不清楚的不对劲」——那些游走的紧绷、那种永远飘离的感觉、那个怎么睡都睡不够的疲惫——都有了名字。

有了名字，就有了方向。有了方向，疗愈才真正开始。

content.en:
India's medical heritage includes two ancient systems: Ayurveda (also known as the "Science of Life") and Siddha medicine.

Ayurveda is considered the oldest holistic medical system in the world. For over five thousand years, it has been practiced in countless traditional Indian households, and its influence has spread to nearly every medical tradition across the globe. This is why Ayurveda is often called the "Mother of All Medicine." Early texts reveal that Ayurvedic physicians possessed remarkable insight into the healing properties of plants — making them forerunners of modern pharmacology. They also had a deep understanding of the body's inner workings; there is even evidence that Ayurvedic practitioners performed surgical procedures. From ancient times to today, this system has consistently emphasized the importance of diet and spirituality. Its principles can be seen echoed in Traditional Chinese Medicine and in the methods of Hippocrates, the "Father of Modern Medicine."

Ayurvedic traditional medicine dates back to the Vedic period around 5000 BCE. It stands as the world's oldest recorded comprehensive medical system.

The Eight Branches of Ayurveda:

1. Kayachikitsa — Internal Medicine
2. Shalakya Tantra — Head & Neck Surgery, Ophthalmology, ENT
3. Shalya Tantra — General Surgery
4. Agada Tantra — Toxicology
5. Bhuta Vidya — Psychiatry
6. Kaumarabhritya — Pediatrics
7. Rasayana — Anti-aging & Rejuvenation
8. Vajikarana — Reproductive Medicine

These eight branches were first described in the Atreya Samhita and continue to be applied in practice today.

What is the relationship between Ayurveda and Yoga?
Both originate from Samkhya philosophy — the science of human evolution. Both traditions hold that all of existence is made up of five great elements: Ether, Air, Fire, Water, and Earth. Within living beings, these five elements give rise to three fundamental energies: Kapha (Earth), Pitta (Fire), and Vata (Air/Wind).

![Five Elements — Pancha Mahabhuta](/images/ayurveda/five-elements.png)

Two paths, one destination:
Yoga and Ayurveda, along with their various therapeutic practices, offer a wide range of health benefits — from stress relief and weight management to improved mood, lower blood pressure, and even the potential reversal of conditions like diabetes and certain cancers. By following the principles of both Yoga and Ayurveda, living in harmony with nature and the seasons, practitioners can enjoy greater physical and mental wellbeing, deepen their yoga and meditation practice, and maintain a graceful, youthful vitality.

Yoga and Ayurveda are best understood as complementary partners. Yoga works through physical and mental practice to bring the body and mind into balance. Ayurveda approaches this through diet, essential oils, herbs, therapeutic treatments, and spices — restoring the body's original Dosha equilibrium from the inside out.

The Three Life Energies of Ayurveda

VATA — Ether + Air
PITTA — Fire + Water
KAPHA — Earth + Water

VATA
The Lightest Energy
Wind Energy (VATA)

Vata governs all movement, function, and connection in the body. It carries qualities of lightness, mobility, cold, dryness, clarity, and irregularity — much like the wind itself.

People with a dominant Vata constitution tend to be slender with lower endurance. They may be prone to dry skin, cold hands and feet, and digestive irregularities. Personality-wise, they are bright and cheerful, optimistic, and imaginative. They are quick to understand and highly adaptable, but may lack staying power. Anxiety and worry can arise easily, and they tend to move and walk at a fast pace.

For yoga, forward folds are especially beneficial — they quiet the mind and draw energy inward. Meditation and Savasana (deep rest) are equally valuable for calming the naturally restless Vata mind.

![Vata — Wind Energy, Air + Space](/images/ayurveda/vata.png)

PITTA
The Steady Energy
Fire Energy (PITTA)

Pitta governs transformation and metabolic processes. It embodies heat, sharpness, lightness, intensity, and flow — qualities that evoke fire.

Those with a dominant Pitta constitution tend to have a medium build, feel heat easily, and perspire readily. They may experience digestive sensitivities or skin issues. Pitta types are passionate and intellectual, courageous and natural leaders. However, they can be quick-tempered and perfectionistic, with a moderate level of sustained energy. They are precise and rule-following in their actions.

When Pitta becomes imbalanced, irritability and sharp emotions tend to flare up. Heart-opening postures — chest openers and backbends — are the most balancing yoga practices for Pitta types.

![Pitta — Fire Energy](/images/ayurveda/pitta.png)

KAPHA
The Heaviest Energy
Water Energy (KAPHA)

Kapha governs structure, form, weight, and density. Its qualities — heaviness, softness, coolness, slowness, and moisture — evoke the nature of water and earth.

People with a dominant Kapha constitution tend to have a sturdy, solid build and are prone to weight gain. Because of the higher internal moisture, respiratory issues may arise. Kapha types have excellent endurance and stamina — they are calm, grounded, big-hearted, and deeply compassionate. They are gentle and devoted, willing to sacrifice for others. While slower to grasp things, their understanding is thorough. They move slowly, have strong patience, and can become deeply attached to people and possessions.

When Kapha falls out of balance, lethargy and low motivation can set in. Energising practices like Sun Salutations (Surya Namaskar) are ideal. For respiratory health, poses like Camel Pose help open the chest and improve breathing.

![Kapha — Water + Earth Energy](/images/ayurveda/kapha.jpg)

Your Innate Dosha (Prakriti) and How It Can Shift

Each person's Dosha constitution is determined at the moment of birth — even at the moment of conception. However, over time, external factors such as diet, daily routines, environment, seasonal changes, and lifestyle can cause the energies to fall out of balance.

"Balance" in Ayurveda does not mean equal amounts of Vata, Pitta, and Kapha. Rather, it refers to the unique "golden ratio" of these three energies as they were at the time of birth. This is your personal equilibrium. When the current state of your energies diverges significantly from this original blueprint, a person may become excessively anxious or deeply lethargic.

Most people have one or two dominant doshas. The three energies can become weakened or aggravated by poor food combinations, overconsumption of certain foods, seasonal shifts, lack of movement, overwork, and late nights.

Doshas and the Stages of Life

Ages 0–25: Kapha is dominant — frequent colds, coughs, and runny noses are common.
Ages 25–50: Pitta takes over — digestive issues, inflammation, and overheating arise.
Age 50+: Vata governs aging — insomnia increases, sleep becomes lighter, menstruation reduces, and joints stiffen. Keeping Vata stable is fundamentally an act of anti-aging.

When Vata becomes severely imbalanced, the body loses internal moisture, leading to premature aging — visible as dry, dehydrated skin. Replenishing the water element is key: quality fats, pure water, and nourishing oils.

Oil therapies (Abhyanga) are highly beneficial. On a mental level, cultivating Kapha's watery, grounding quality helps to neutralise Vata's airy restlessness.

Vata is closely linked to the nervous system. Keeping Vata calm supports emotional stability and inner health. As the Huangdi Neijing (Yellow Emperor's Classic) reminds us, emotions — and the nervous system behind them — are at the root of many illnesses. Emotional wellbeing is, therefore, essential to whole health.

印度的医学体系包括阿育吠陀（Ayurveda，又称生命吠陀）医学和悉达（Siddha）医学。

它被认为是世界上最古老的医学体系。五千多年时，它在无数印度传统家庭中使用着。其影响波及南北半球几乎所有的医学系统。因此印度阿育吠陀被誉为“医疗之母”。由早期的文献可看出，阿育吠陀的医生对于植物的强力医疗特性具有先知灼见，可以说是现代药理学的开山鼻祖。他们也对体内的运作极为了解，甚至有证据指出阿育吠陀医师动过人体手术。此外，此系统从古到今都同样强调饮食与灵性的重要性，中国的中医以及“现时代医学之父”希波克拉底（Hippocrates）的医疗方法，都可见到阿育吠陀的影子。

阿育吠陀传统医学可以追溯到公元前5000年的吠陀时代。它以世界上最古老的有记载的综合医学体系而著称。



以下为阿育吠陀的八大分支：

1. Kayachikitsa（内科学）
2. Shalakya Tantra（头颈外科学及治疗、眼科学和耳鼻喉科学）
3. Shalya Tantra（外科学）
4. Agada Tantra（毒物学）
5. Bhuta Vidya（精神病学）
6. Kaumarabhritya（儿科学）
7. Rasayana（延缓身体老化的抗衰学科）
8. Vajikarana（生育学）

上述八大分支最早的论述出现在《阿提耶集》（Atreya Samhita）中，它至今仍然在现实生活中应用。

阿育吠陀和瑜伽是什么关系？
他们两者都源自于数论派哲学（研究人类演化的科学），他们都认为万物由五大元素组成：空，风，火，水，土，而这五大元素在生命体内演化出了三种能量：Kapha（土）Pitta（火）Vata（风）。

![五大元素 Pancha Mahabhuta](/images/ayurveda/five-elements.png)



万法归一，相同点：
Yoga 和阿育吠陀理论及其各种治疗方法可以为健康带来各种各样的好处，从缓解压力到预防体重增加，改善情绪，降低高血压，甚至逆转糖尿病和癌症。遵循瑜伽和阿育吠陀的原则，与自然和季节和谐共处，练习者可以享受更好的身心健康，从而改善他们的瑜伽和冥想练习，保持优雅和年轻的状态。

瑜伽和阿育吠陀更像是可以互相合作相互调节。一个是通过身体及心灵上的练习达到一个平衡的状态，而阿育吠陀更多是从饮食、精油、草药、SPA、香料等各个方面去让身体原始 Dosha 能量达到初始状态。



阿育吠陀三大生命能量

VATA -- Ether + Air，瓦塔 -- 空 + 风
PITTA -- Fire + Water，皮塔 -- 火 + 水
KAPHA -- Earth + Water，卡帕 -- 土 + 水

VATA
最轻的能量
风能（VATA）

特征主管机能、运动、联系的能量。具有轻、动、冷、干燥、透明、不规则等令人联想到风的特质。

风能体质的人体型纤瘦，耐力较为不足。容易有皮肤干燥、手脚冰冷或便秘的毛病。个性开朗活泼，乐观进取，想象力丰富。适应力及理解力佳，但缺乏持续力。容易焦躁、忧虑。行动敏捷，走路的速度也很快。

建议适合的瑜伽动作也是任何有关前弯的体位法，可以沉静心灵；或者是静坐与大休息，同样有助于让漂浮的心平稳下来。



![Vata - 风能量 Air + Space](/images/ayurveda/vata.png)



PITTA
稳健的能量
火能（PITTA）

特征主管机制、转换的能量。具有热、敏锐、轻、辣、流动等令人联想到火的特质。

火能体质的人中等体型，怕热、易流汗，容易拉肚子或有皮肤方面的问题。充满热情和知性，具备勇气和领导者气质。急躁、易怒，完美主义者。持续力中等。动作正确而且守规则。

建议一旦皮塔能量失衡，就容易脾气上来，激动且急性子。适合的瑜伽动作是关于开胸的体位法练习。



![Pitta - 火能量 Fire + Energy](/images/ayurveda/pitta.png)



KAPHA
最重的能量
水能（KAPHA）

特征主管构造、形状、重量、软硬度的能量。具备重、软、冷、慢、湿等令人联想到水的特质。

水能体质的人体格壮硕，易胖。由于体内湿气较重，容易有呼吸系统的问题。体力、持续力佳，沉着稳重，心胸宽大。温柔敦厚，有牺牲奉献的精神。理解速度不快但深入。动作缓慢，忍耐力强。对事物易生执着，有积存事物的习性。

建议卡法一旦失衡可能会变得没有活力，让人觉得懒散。所以适合的瑜伽动作是带来活力的拜日式，而在改善呼吸道方面，可以练习骆驼式等动作。



![Kapha - 水能量 Water + Earth](/images/ayurveda/kapha.jpg)



先天的能量（DOSHA）与后天的能量转换

每个人先天的 Dosha 在出生的那一刻就已经注定了（甚至在受精卵形成的那一刻），但是后天随着饮食作息、周围环境、季节属性等外界因素的影响导致能量失衡。

而所谓的“平衡”状态，并不是说风、火、水这三种能量的等值，而是指一个人出生时候这三种能量的“黄金比例”，才是 TA 独一无二的平衡值。当本身具有的能量与原始的能量（出生时）出现失衡差别甚至完全改变时，人就会变得极度紧张或者极度懒惰。

大多数人往往会有一种或者两种占主导地位，三个能量会由于食物搭配不当、过食某些食物、季节性变化、缺乏运动、超量工作和熬夜等因素而变得虚弱。

年龄与三大特质的关系

0-25 岁：由 Kapha 能量主导，经常咳嗽感冒流鼻涕
25-50 岁：Pitta 能量主导，胃病胃炎、上火
50 岁后：衰老由 Vata 引起，年龄越老化，失眠、睡眠越来越少，经期变少、关节变硬，所以保持 Vata 的稳定，就是在对抗衰老。

若是风行能量很大失衡会导致身体内在水分缺失提前老化，体现在外在皮肤发干。加强水元素的补充，优质脂肪、优质的水、优质的油。



可以适当做油疗，精神层面利用 Kapha 的属性（水属性）来中和 Vata 风属性。

风行能量与神经系统相关，保持风性稳定帮助情绪及内在健康。黄帝内经中提到情绪（背后的神经系统）是很多疾病的起因，所以保持情绪健康很重要。
